documents.abstract: App stores provide a range of health applications for people living with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and Parkinson’s disease (PD). Users like patients can access information from both manufacturer-provided app descriptions and metadata, as well as from user reviews. However, navigating this information to identify value-generating apps of high quality remains challenging. From a health technology assessment (HTA) standpoint, quality is defined by evidence-based medicine, safety, and user-centeredness. To explore the potential value of app store information available to patients, we conducted a descriptive, mixed-methods analysis of unstructured app metadata and user feedback from the Apple App Store and Google Play Store (as of May 2024). We analyzed 1,237 AD/PD-related apps which included 50 duplicates (resulting in 1,187 apps), utilizing descriptive statistics, content analysis, large language model-supported exploratory classification, and a topic modeling approach. In total, only about 2% of the apps claimed to be certified medical devices. Moreover, 24% of Apple apps and 14% of Google apps were in the “Medical” app store genre, among which we found that 63% of Apple and 54% of Google apps were patient-facing. We manually categorized patient-facing apps predominantly under “Care Support,” followed by “Health & Wellness” and “Patient Monitoring.” Importantly, user feedback provided exploratory, potentially valuable patient-reported outcome and experience information but is derived from personal opinions on “user experience,” “health improvement,” and “costs.” As quality information on DHTs could be identified in unstructured app metadata, this information should be improved in trustworthiness and more accessible to users like patients, supporting the public to find high-quality health apps. Furthermore, as user opinions contained information with potential value for patients, these should be explored as complementary value-generating indicators of health apps in future work.

The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus for Artificial General Intelligence (ARC-AGI) is a generative, few-shot fluid intelligence benchmark. Although humans effortlessly solve ARC-AGI, it remains extremely difficult for even the most advanced artificial intelligence systems. Inspired by methods for modelling human intelligence spanning neuroscience to psychology, we propose a cognitively inspired ARC-AGI solver. Our solver integrates System 1 intuitions with System 2 reasoning in an efficient and interpretable process using neurosymbolic methods based on Vector Symbolic Algebras (VSAs). Our solver works by object-centric program synthesis, leveraging VSAs to represent abstract objects, guide solution search, and enable sample-efficient neural learning. Preliminary results indicate success, with our solver scoring 10.8% on ARC-AGI-1-Train and 3.0% on ARC-AGI-1-Eval. Additionally, our solver performs well on simpler benchmarks, scoring 94.5% on Sort-of-ARC and 83.1% on 1D-ARC-the latter outperforming GPT-4 at a tiny fraction of the computational cost. Importantly, our approach is unique; we believe we are the first to apply VSAs to ARC-AGI and have developed one of the most cognitively plausible ARC-AGI solvers yet. Our code is available at: https://github.com/ijoffe/ARC-VSA-2025.

As LLM agents undertake increasingly complex, long-horizon tasks, verifying their outputs becomes increasingly challenging. We study how verification capability can be strengthened with a fixed base model, without access to reference answers or grading rubrics at test time. Repeated sampling yields multiple rollouts that can contain complementary correct claims, but we need a reliable verification mechanism to determine which claims to trust. We first find that disagreement often exposes correct alternatives, while consensus can conceal errors. These observations motivate VeriHarness, which turns the underlying LLM a generator uses into an agentic verifier by giving it a workspace, evidence tools, and reusable verification skills. A disagreement resolver checks competing claims against environmental evidence, while a consensus challenger tests shared claims and searches for omitted requirements. Their findings guide the selection and revision of the final artifact. Across five long-horizon workspace benchmarks and two frontier models, VeriHarness achieves the highest selection scores among the evaluated baselines. Evidence-backed revision further improves average performance, bringing gains over a single rollout to 6.2 points with Gemini 3.5 Flash and 6.4 points with Claude Opus 4.8. We further show that verification skills can self-improve from failure feedback, demonstrating VeriHarness as a novel and critical approach for scaling long-horizon agentic verification. We release the full pool of approximately 26,000 rollouts across all five benchmarks and both models, produced at a cost of over $100,000, to support future research on agentic verification.

Digital transformation is increasingly shaping the ways in which people remember and grieve. While existing platforms and social networks primarily preserve static content, immersive environments such as the metaverse and advances in generative artificial intelligence (AI) enable the creation of interactive, AI-based memory avatars, often also referred to as “griefbots” or “deadbots”. This study examines the perceptions, acceptance, opportunities, as well as psychosocial and ethical limitations of such avatars from the perspective of potential users. To provide an empirical foundation, an interactive prototype was developed and evaluated as part of a quantitative study (N = 33). These results were supplemented by qualitative guided interviews with experts in grief counseling, psychotherapy, and pastoral care. The findings paint a highly ambivalent picture: While respondents see potential in preserving life stories or in processing missed goodbyes, concerns regarding emotional dependence, difficulties in accepting loss, and ethical and data protection risks dominate. The Behavioral Intention to use the technology depends largely on Perceived Usefulness (r = 0.74) and Emotional Impact (r = 0.82), rather than purely on user interface elements. Experts emphasize that simulated interactions must not hinder the necessary process of letting go. The study concludes with recommendations for transparency requirements, time limits, and clear ethical safeguards for vulnerable groups.

Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MRAG) has emerged as a reliable and cost-effective technique of grounding the generative capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) into relevant, up-to-date, external knowledge. Despite presenting several benefits, such as reducing hallucinatory behavior, they also introduce new attack surfaces, including leakage of private information and vulnerabilities against data extraction attacks. In this paper, we introduce $\immrag$, an adaptive and automatic data extraction attack procedure operating in a black box setting against \emph{image-returning} MRAG, a configuration in which the retrieved visual artifact is itself the response. Each query blends an attacker-held shadow image with an image already recovered from the system, and relevance-weighted resampling steers subsequent queries towards regions of the embedding space that still yield novel retrievals. Unlike current extraction attacks that aim to persuade the model towards data leakage by placing a malicious query as a textual prompt, $\immrag$ embeds the malicious instructions inside a user-given input image. We evaluate $\immrag$ on three plausible and distinct real-world scenarios: medical assistant, document-focused helper and general purpose tool. The experiments involve the study of the effectiveness of the attack on multiple CLIP-family retrievers, as well as the impact of various generators. A single 2500-query run reconstructs up to 611 distinct radiology images, 566 document scans and 416 general-purpose images under local-feature correspondence, and reaches up to $5.6\times$ as many distinct datastore items as a non-adaptive baseline. Our results show the urgent need for safeguards specifically designed for multimodal data.

Exoskeletons are increasingly used to reduce physical strain in manual material handling, yet their true influence on worker exertion and fatigue remains challenging to quantify due to the lack of scalable and objective assessment methods. This study introduces a wearable-sensor framework that links subjective workload perception to quantifiable biomechanical responses during realistic industrial tasks, performed with (Exo) and without (NoExo) passive shoulder exoskeleton assistance. Twenty participants completed three representative tasks including loading, overhead screwing, and palletizing, while wearing ten IMUs positioned on the upper trapezius, deltoids, biceps, lumbar erector spinae, and hamstrings. Accelerometer signals (at 148 Hz) were converted to magnitude, segmented into 0.5 s windows with 50% overlap, and reduced to six biomechanical features per sensor, yielding 60 features per window. The dataset comprised 36,901 NoExo and 38,023 Exo windows, each labeled through task-specific Borg-scale mappings. Machine-learning models were evaluated using Leave-One-Participant-Out cross-validation. Random Forest and XGBoost achieved the highest performance (median accuracy = 0.83, F1-weighted = 0.82), outperforming Logistic Regression and Linear Discriminant Analysis. Exoskeleton use decreased inter-participant variability and reduced misclassifications, with top models reaching near-perfect separability for several individuals ( A U C > 0 . 9 5 ). Feature-importance analyses consistently identified the lower back and hamstrings as the most informative sensor locations, enabling up to a 70% reduction in sensor count with minimal performance degradation. Critically, the proportion of hard-exertion windows decreased by nearly 75% with exoskeleton assistance, demonstrating measurable ergonomic benefit. These results establish a deployment-ready approach for real-time, objective assessment of physical workload in manufacturing environments. The proposed framework advances scalable evaluation of assistive technologies, supports data-driven ergonomic design and training, and offers the first evidence that wearable IMU-based machine-learning models can reliably quantify exoskeleton effectiveness in complex, real-world occupational settings.

This study aimed to analyze perceptions of well-being, happiness, and meaning in life among non-indigenous and indigenous participants from the Javaé and Karajá peoples, based on etic and emic perspectives. A qualitative, exploratory, and comparative design was adopted. Participants included 13 indigenous students enrolled in the intercultural education degree program at the Federal University of Goiás and 14 non-indigenous individuals living in the central-west region of Brazil. Data were collected through three open-ended questions addressing well-being, happiness, and meaning in life. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using initial and focused coding procedures grounded in constructivist grounded theory, supported by computational tools based on large language models. The findings revealed common categories across both groups, such as family and community relationships, meaningful work and teaching, physical and mental health, and realization of aspirations. However, these categories acquire distinct meanings across different cultural frameworks. Among indigenous participants, well-being was conceived as a relational, collective, and territorially grounded experience, integrating culture, spirituality, ancestry, and nature. In contrast, non-indigenous participants emphasized more individualized narratives, centered on personal progress, consumption, and immediate pleasures. These results highlight the importance of intercultural and decolonial approaches to psychological research on well-being and challenge the universalization of models derived predominantly from WEIRD populations.

Who or what is conscious? Because subjective experience is directly accessible only in the first person, judgments about consciousness in other entities depend partly on analogy. Historically, such inferences have focused on nonhuman animals, but advances in artificial intelligence have raised the possibility of conscious AI. Here we develop a causal framework for evaluating such evidential analogies. The key distinction is between similarities in factors plausibly involved in generating consciousness and similarities in downstream behavioural or cognitive effects. Our framework weights source-target similarity by causal relevance while allowing for unknown causes, disabling differences and alternative routes to consciousness. Applied to biological systems, it explains why analogical support generally weakens with increasing causal distance from humans. Applied to contemporary AI, it suggests that behavioural similarity provides only limited evidence for consciousness because relevant causal correspondences remain poorly established. The framework also clarifies what evidence would strengthen claims of artificial consciousness.

As LLMs take up the role of authoring charts using visualization domain-specific languages (DSLs), the human constraints that shaped those languages may no longer apply, as what is easy for a person is not necessarily easy for a model. To understand how LLMs might work better with DSLs, we explore where and how they fail with current DSL designs. We evaluate 10 JSON-style visualization DSLs with 41 tasks across 3 LLMs, then assess the generated specifications with JSON and rendering checks, and qualitative coding of failed cases. Analyzing how this specification generation process fails, we identify four recurring failure patterns, link each to specific DSL features, and discuss design considerations for future DSL designs.

On-policy self-distillation has recently emerged as an effective approach for improving language-model reasoning by supervising students with a frozen or EMA version of themselves that receives privileged information. Its application to multimodal large language models (MLLMs), however, remains largely unexplored. Recent approaches use privileged visual information, such as image crops corresponding to a question, to improve fine-grained perception, but their gains are confined to tasks that benefit from such visual zooming and require either human-annotated grounding data or external teacher models. We introduce a different form of on-policy self-distillation for MLLMs that provides the teacher with textual, spatially grounded guidance identifying the visual elements relevant to a query. We use procedurally generated scenes with automatically available object identities and spatial coordinates, enabling scalable and annotation-free post-training. The teacher uses this spatial guidance to locate and integrate evidence from multiple relevant image regions, while the student learns to reproduce the resulting behavior from the image and question alone. Our approach consistently improves performance on counting, document and chart understanding benchmarks across multiple models. Importantly, although post-training uses only synthetic scenes, the resulting improvements transfer to real-world perception benchmarks, yielding a 3.23-point gain in average performance across CVBench, V*, ZoomBench, BLINK, HR-Bench, and MME-RealWorld. These results show that spatially grounded privileged information can induce broader perceptual capabilities through on-policy self-distillation, enabling substantial synthetic-to-real transfer beyond the task and data distribution used for post-training. ABSTRACT Background The rapid spread of visual misinformation online, intensified by advances in generative artificial intelligence, presents new challenges for adolescents' digital information literacy. Although students' difficulties in evaluating online information are well documented, little is known about how they assess different forms of visual misinformation on social media. Objectives This study examined the extent to which lower secondary school students can successfully identify different types of visual misinformation on social media, the evaluation strategies they use, and whether these strategies predict misinformation detection across types of visual misinformation. Methods The participants were 272 students in Grades 7–9 who evaluated social media posts containing visual misinformation, including manipulated videos, manipulated images, and AI‐generated images. Students rated each item's credibility and provided written justifications. Evaluation strategies were coded using a theoretically grounded scheme. Results Students were moderately successful in identifying manipulated images and videos, but struggled to detect AI‐generated images, which were often perceived as credible. Students relied primarily on evaluation of visual appearance and content, while source evaluation and corroboration strategies were infrequently used. Across all visual misinformation types, examination of visual features, knowledge‐based evaluation, sourcing, and corroboration strategies predicted misinformation detection. However, corroboration was the only strategy that reliably predicted identification of AI‐generated images. Conclusions Students mostly rely on first‐hand evaluation of visual appearance and content, but these strategies are inadequate for detecting realistic AI‐generated visual misinformation. Instruction should emphasize active verification strategies, particularly corroboration, and support students in coordinating multiple evaluation strategies when engaging with online visual information.

The Zircon Firefly is a breakthrough aerial VTOL platform, sovereign aerial vehicle, and advanced unmanned aircraft system (UAS / UAV) engineered to deploy next-generation firefighting drone and fire fighting drones technology at scale. Designed to operate as an autonomous small drone or coordinated autonomous large aircraft singularly or within a high-density swarm powered by AI swarm intelligence, the aircraft redefines global wildfire mitigation, bushfire suppression, bush fire fighting, fire prevention, fire management, and community safety. Being developed through rigorous digital twin modeling, CFD simulation, and aerodynamic evaluation of R&D prototyping, the platform replaces traditional, low-efficiency water bombing with continuous thrust-based suppression and Mechanical Flame Separation (MFS)—conceptually scaling the ground-proven leaf blower tactic into a high-performance aerospace defence force.Engineered to eliminate the critical "suppression gap" where traditional aircraft drop payloads and leave fire lines to refill, this high-powered platform utilizes massive, high-velocity airflow generated by commercial jet turbines and high-thrust Electric Ducted Fans (EDFs). This delivers persistent atmospheric inerting, combustion disruption, low-oxygen flame suppression, and high-velocity airflow suppression across any burning forest or grassland ecosystem. Operating as a waterless firefighting solution that delivers zero-chemical fire suppression, the Firefly executes high-capacity perimeter defence, Urban-Wildland Interface (WUI) shielding, and direct convective updraft penetration while maintaining complete thermal turbulence stability via a proprietary gyroscopic stabilization assembly.Built for versatility across all operational phases, the platform excels at rapid initial attack, high-intensity fire management, fuel load reduction, controlled prescribed burn containment, and indigenous cultural burn management. Real-time operational intelligence is driven by multi-spectral sensor fusion—integrating UV sensors for ultraviolet flame detection, LIDAR, Doppler radar, thermal imaging, multi-spectral optical sensors, satellite communications, 5G connectivity, and direct data links with deployed ground sensors. These systems will enable both piloted or fully autonomous systems including precise beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS) operations for unmanned or uncrewed platforms, total real-time situational awareness through collision avoidance, provide extended flight endurance, and rapid five-minute in-field turnaround logistics.By suppressing major mega-fires before forest canopy destruction, the platform accelerates carbon reduction, curbing gigatons of wildfire CO2 carbon emissions, providing a massive carbon emission offset, protecting critical terrestrial carbon sinks, and preserving biodiversity, forest canopy preservation, ecosystem resilience, watershed protection, and catchment defence.As a patented sovereign technology and essential emergency services technology, the Firefly safeguards critical assets—offering non-stop critical infrastructure protection, utility corridor defence, power substation protection, and renewable energy asset protection. By mitigating catastrophic fire spread, the platform directly drives avoided loss economics, disaster loss reduction, disaster risk reduction, and climate adaptation. This delivers significant government expenditure reduction, insurance risk mitigation, insurance rate stabilization, and substantial economic cost reduction on a global scale.

Generative AI can support writing, but frictionless access may cause cognitive offloading before users develop their own ideas. We introduce Engage-to-Unlock, a productive-friction mechanism that unlocks generative capabilities after users meaningfully engage with the task. In a controlled experiment (N = 398), participants completed a writing task under one of four conditions: Human-Only, Standard Chatbot, Engage-to-Unlock, or Time-Matched Unlock, which matched unlock timing to Engage-to-Unlock participants but independent of users' engagement, then evaluated passages for evidence and inferential errors. Results show that Engage-to-Unlock redistributed effort across tasks: participants spent more time writing and less time evaluating, without increasing overall task duration. They also submitted more prompts than in other AI-assisted conditions and showed the highest accuracy-per-time evaluation efficiency across conditions. These findings suggest that designing GenAI access to encourage early human engagement may provide a productive form of friction, while retaining active AI use and efficient downstream evaluation.

documents.abstract: The rapid digital transformation of the pharmaceutical sector has created a growing demand for professionals who can combine pharmaceutical knowledge with computational and data-analytic skills. Python programming has emerged as a valuable educational and professional tool because of its simple syntax, open-source nature, extensive scientific libraries, and applicability in data analysis, visualization, automation, pharmacokinetics, pharmacovigilance, formulation research, clinical studies, bioinformatics, quality control, and artificial intelligence-assisted drug development. The revised B.Pharm curriculum introduced by the Pharmacy Council of India under the NEP 2020 framework recognizes this changing professional environment by including Basics of Python Programming for Pharmaceutical Sciences at the undergraduate level. This curricular development represents an important shift from conventional computer literacy toward structured programming, pharmaceutical data handling, scientific visualization, and computational problem-solving. The present review examines the rationale for incorporating Python programming into pharmaceutical education and correlates the revised curriculum with emerging requirements of the pharmaceutical industry. Particular emphasis is placed on the relevance of NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, data cleaning, CSV/Excel processing, pharmacokinetic datasets, adverse drug reaction analysis, dissolution-profile visualization, research data management, and introductory pathways toward machine learning and artificial intelligence. The review further discusses the potential contribution of Python competency to pharmaceutical research and development, quality assurance, manufacturing, regulatory science, clinical research, pharmacovigilance, and Pharma 4.0. Challenges related to faculty training, infrastructure, limited instructional hours, data integrity, validation, and responsible use of artificial intelligence are also considered. It is concluded that Python should not be regarded merely as an additional programming subject in the pharmacy curriculum, but as a foundational digital competency capable of improving data literacy, research capability, interdisciplinary collaboration, and industrial readiness among future pharmacy graduates. This article cover subject wisr role of python programming in pharmaceutical industries.

The increasing incidence of wild animal intrusion in agricultural areas poses significant risks to both human safety and crop productivity. This project, AI-IoT Smart Animal Surveillance for Human Safety, proposes a real-time monitoring system that integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI) with Internet of Things (IoT) to detect, alert, and assess the presence of wild animals near farms. The system utilises a Raspberry Pi equipped with a camera module and employs the YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once) object detection algorithm to accurately identify animals from live video feeds. Upon detection, the system captures the image, sends an email alert with timestamp and location to the farmer, and activates a buzzer to warn nearby individuals. Additionally, IoT-based health monitoring sensors such as temperature, heartbeat, and gas sensors are used to evaluate the physical condition and surrounding environment of the detected animals, aiding early detection of diseases or environmental threats. The system operates in real-time and ensures quick response to critical situations, thereby minimizing crop damage and reducing the risk of human-animal conflicts. It is designed to be cost-effective, energy-efficient, and easy to deploy in rural and remote areas. Furthermore, the system can be enhanced with features such as mobile application integration, cloud-based data storage, and GPS tracking for better monitoring and control. Overall, the proposed system provides a smart, automated, and reliable solution for wildlife surveillance and safety management.

This research WIP paper presents DBWorkout, a web-based platform that supports formative SQL learning through sandbox-based execution, automated result-based feedback, and session-based gamification. Learning Structured Query Language (SQL) remains challenging for undergraduate students due to limited opportunities for interactive practice and immediate feedback. Students iteratively practice SQL on live database instances while receiving multi-dimensional feedback on query correctness, including row values, column structure, and ordering. To reduce instructor workload, DBWorkout incorporates large language model (LLM)-assisted tools for schema and task generation within a human-in-the-loop workflow. A pilot study with teaching assistants and a classroom deployment involving 170 undergraduate students across two in-class sessions show strong perceived learning value (90% agreement) and engagement (87% enjoyment), alongside low reported pressure (22%). However, only 42% of students found the automated feedback sufficiently actionable, a finding independently corroborated by 40% of open-ended responses raising feedback quality concerns, providing cross-method triangulation of this gap. These findings demonstrate the technical feasibility and early pedagogical potential of DBWorkout while identifying directions for enhancing feedback quality and supporting sustained SQL learning.

documents.abstract: This article examines the role and pedagogical potential of aphorisms and words of wisdom in the spiritual and moral upbringing of a child. Concise yet profoundly meaningful aphorisms exert a powerful influence on instilling virtues such as goodness, kindness, patience, gratitude, humility, honesty, the pursuit of knowledge, and self-awareness in a child's heart. The paper conducts a pedagogical analysis of selected aphorisms from Anvar Ahmad’s work “Encyclopedia of Wisdom: Aphorisms Leading to Happiness.” Particular emphasis is placed on the psychological impact of these aphorisms on primary school pupils, their practical integration into daily life, and opportunities for collaborative application within the student–teacher–parent paradigm. Wisdom is interpreted not as ready-made didactic preaching, but as a spiritual tool that cultivates critical thinking, situational awareness, and constructive independent reflection.

This chapter examines the rapidly changing realities confronting the wildland firefighting workforce as climate change produces longer fire seasons, larger and more extreme wildfires, and increasingly complex operational demands. It considers how repeated exposure to intense heat, hazardous smoke, difficult terrain, long deployments, and unpredictable fire behavior affects the people responsible for protecting communities, ecosystems, and critical infrastructure. These environmental and operational pressures intersect with persistent workforce challenges, including difficulties in recruitment and retention, uneven access to training, staffing shortages, inadequate compensation, limited career pathways, and inconsistent institutional support.Drawing on research in wildland fire operations, human performance, occupational health, and workforce management, the chapter assesses the cumulative effects of these conditions on firefighters’ physical safety, mental health, job performance, family lives, and long-term career decisions. Particular attention is given to fatigue, injury, respiratory and cardiovascular risks, trauma, burnout, and the organizational cultures that may discourage personnel from seeking help. The discussion also considers how temporary employment structures, geographic disparities, and barriers affecting underrepresented groups can undermine workforce resilience and institutional knowledge.The chapter concludes by identifying evidence-based strategies for building a safer, stronger, and more sustainable workforce. These include competitive pay and benefits, clearer professional standards, expanded training and leadership development, improved health monitoring, accessible mental health services, predictable scheduling, and stronger pathways to permanent employment. It also highlights policy reforms needed to modernize workforce systems, strengthen accountability, and ensure that wildland firefighters receive resources and recognition commensurate with roles that are becoming more critical—and more demanding—each passing year.

Abstract Workplace health investment is a firm-level public health practice through which organizations protect workers, reduce occupational-health risks and maintain the health-related capacity of the workforce. Using 12,669 firm-year observations of Chinese A-share non-financial listed firms from 2013 to 2024, this study constructs a sentence-level CSR text measure of workplace health investment and examines its association with employment growth and employment adjustment volatility. The results show that workplace health investment is positively associated with employment growth and employment adjustment volatility. A one-standard-deviation increase in workplace health investment raises employment growth by about 2.4 percentage points and increases adjustment volatility by about 0.012. Mechanism tests show that workplace health investment reduces work-injury rates, employee turnover and vacancy-filling duration, and that the increase in adjustment volatility is concentrated in positive adjustment and industry upturns. The findings indicate that workplace health governance may support employment resilience by reducing preventable health-related labor frictions and strengthening expansion-oriented employment adjustment when demand conditions are favorable.

documents.abstract: Introduction Family and domestic violence (FDV), which includes intimate partner and family violence, affects workplace safety through spillover impacts on workers, organisations, and occupational health systems. To date, workplace interventions addressing the issue of FDV have predominantly concentrated on providing support to victim-survivors, while there is limited research regarding employer responses to employees who perpetrate such violence. Method A scoping review was conducted following Arksey and O’Malley’s framework and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines, which examined existing evidence from workplace policies, practices, and organisational mechanisms addressing FDV perpetration by workers. Peer-reviewed studies and high-quality grey literature on workplace responses to perpetration of FDV were systematically searched across multiple databases and online sources, and 28 documents on workplace responses to FDV perpetration were analysed. Results Findings from the scoping review reveal four dominant insights across the literature: 1. Perpetration of FDV is a major workplace problem, yet responses are under-researched; 2. Workplaces employ wide-ranging and varied responses, from zero tolerance dismissal of perpetrators to responsibility avoidance; 3. Responses lack a solid evidence-base and regulatory frameworks to address the problem remain weak; 4. Practical strategies are provided to better manage risk, strengthen safety, and reduce violence. Conclusion Our findings underscore the need for clearer organisational guidance, evidence-based strategies, and robust regulatory frameworks to strengthen workplace responses to FDV perpetration and improve occupational safety outcomes. Practical applications Effective workplace responses to perpetration of FDV should consider work design factors, referral pathways and confidentiality protections which are guided by graduated accountability models and regulatory frameworks.

Be is a proposed organization dedicated to making safe, professionally governed artificial intelligence emotional support freely accessible to people who need someone to talk to. Be proposes an AI emotional-support system designed around a foundational distinction: an AI must never confuse what it observes with what it infers. Version 2.0 further develops the proposal's framework for adaptive conversational communication through the principle Adaptive Tone, Fixed Boundaries. Be may adapt its tone, vocabulary, pacing, humor, warmth, and conversational style to meet an individual where they are, while maintaining fixed ethical and relational boundaries. The system should allow human-like communication without creating a false human identity, adapting the interface without fabricating the relationship. The proposal incorporates Red Tape Theory™ as a proposed safety methodology: Observe. Record. Question. Do not force the axiom. Interpretation must never be represented as observation. Be does not propose to diagnose users or replace licensed mental-health professionals. Instead, it proposes a professionally governed pathway through which an AI system may recognize when AI-only support may no longer be an appropriate level of support and facilitate access to human care. A proposed charitable human-care program, If You Get It, You Get It, would seek to use charitable resources to help people access licensed professional care when professionally established safety criteria indicate that additional human support may be appropriate. Version 2.0 expands the proposal's treatment of personalization as a safety boundary, including the distinction between adapting communication to an individual and constructing a misleading simulated relationship. It also addresses clinical governance, privacy, autonomy, human handoff, crisis safety, documentation, intellectual-property considerations, research and evaluation, and a potential future child-focused system provisionally called NewBee. This publication is a founding proposal and does not represent a deployed clinical service, licensed mental-health treatment program, clinical efficacy claim, professional endorsement, or completed charitable program. Be begins with the question: Where could this harm somebody?

Те стигат до извод в три стъпки: изоставането в производителността е вътре в отраслите и е най-голямо при местните фирми; при нововъведенията то е най-голямо в организацията на работата, а не в продуктите; вероятна причина е прекъснатият частен организационен капитал. Самото управление обаче не е измерено пряко. Бележката пита дали публичните институции могат да намалят времето и цената за придобиване на организационен капитал, без да заместват пазарния подбор. Предлага „институционална инфраструктура за организационен капитал“: доброволна диагностика, стандартни управленски инструменти, практическо консултиране, по-малка административна тежест за участниците и помощ при преструктуриране, продажба или прекратяване на фирмата. Показва, че процедурата по стабилизация в Търговския закон съществува от 2017 г., но между 2017 и 2022 г. е използвана само 12 пъти. Два полеви експеримента подкрепят управленското консултиране, но ефектите силно се различават между програмите. Затова бележката не предлага национална програма, а три пилота с предварително заявени критерии за оценка и прекратяване. Подготвена с помощта на ChatGPT (OpenAI) и Claude (Anthropic); числата са сверени с посочените източници. Пълен текст на български. This working note follows two earlier notes on Bulgaria's income distribution and on the historical layers of its economy. They reach a three-step conclusion: the productivity gap lies within sectors and is largest among domestically controlled firms; in innovation, the gap is widest in the organisation of work rather than in products; a likely cause is the interrupted stock of private organisational capital, although management itself has not been measured directly. The note asks whether public institutions can reduce the time and cost of acquiring organisational capital without replacing market selection. It proposes an "institutional infrastructure for organisational capital": voluntary firm diagnostics, standard management tools, practical consulting, lower administrative burden for participants, and help with restructuring, transfer or exit. It shows that Bulgaria's pre-insolvency stabilisation procedure has existed since 2017 but was used only 12 times between 2017 and 2022. Two field experiments support management consulting, but effects vary widely across programmes. The note therefore proposes three pilots with pre-registered evaluation and termination criteria rather than a national programme. Prepared with the assistance of ChatGPT (OpenAI) and Claude (Anthropic). Full text in Bulgarian.

Protocol」の完全な実装体系を提示するものである。 超知能AI(Superintelligent AI)の台頭と敵対的機械学習攻撃の高度化に対し、論理層でのエラー訂正(FEC)やソフトウェア的ガードレールによる防御は、指数関数的なエントロピー生成(ランダウアーの原理)と計算量的バイパスを許す致命的な脆弱性を抱えている。これに対し、本アーキテクチャは「情報は物理的である」というテーゼに回帰し、以下の4つの物理防壁を構築する: 物理層の非可逆的防衛(1e-12 BERの熱力学的関所): Abstract The rapid development of digital technologies has transformed modern society in almost every sphere of human life. The growth of the internet, smartphones, social media, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, big data, digital payments, e-commerce, and online education has created what is commonly described as a digital society. Digital technologies have improved communication, access to information, education, healthcare, business, public administration, and economic participation. At the same time, the increasing dependence on digital systems has created significant ethical challenges relating to privacy, data protection, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, misinformation, digital inequality, online harassment, intellectual property, surveillance, and the responsible use of emerging technologies.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Abstract- Brick’s manufacturing is an important industry in India. Bricks are very important raw material required in construction. Thousands of construction projects are ongoing in Mumbai Economic zone and thane district. Bricks manufacturers in thane district are primary suppliers of bricks to these construction sites. Large number of tribal communities from thane district are engaged as bricks worker in Bricks manufacturing Industry. These Tribal Brick workers play an important role in the construction industry, providing the foundation for buildings, homes, and other infrastructure projects. Despite their significant contribution, they have very challenging lives. Harsh physical labour, prolong working hours, and limited resources is an everyday issue for these workers. These tribal workers have lack of formal education, which limits their employment opportunities outside the brick industry. These workers Often employed on a seasonal basis, with very low wages, long working hours, and. Due to illiteracy and poor economic condition times, they often exploited by their owners. This article will focus on the working and living conditions of brick workers in the Thane district. This research aims to understand the socio-economic status and problems, occupational health issues, and the impact of their work environment on their overall well-being of Tribal Bricks Wokers. This paper is going to focus on the problems and possible remedies to address the various issues of Tribal Brick Workers. This research will be helpful to the broader discourse on informal labours problems and provides a foundation for policymakers and social organizations to address the challenges faced by brick workers.
topics: Social and Economic Development in India

documents.abstract: When a person approves an action while tired, the AI agent that carries it out may send a message that cannot be taken back, a refund, an alert, an account change. This note suggests a simple fix: before sending, check if the approving person showed signs of fatigue. If so, hold the message briefly for a second look before it goes out. This applies to any communication platform that sends such messages on behalf of a human or an AI agent, including Zoho CPaaS, Twilio, and Infobip.

documents.abstract: Natural disasters demand rapid synthesis of fragmented, heterogeneous data often distributed across independently governed organizations. This paper introduces DisasterAI, a federated, cloud-native, and multi-modal AI architecture for disaster intelligence. Unlike centralized analytics platforms, DisasterAI emphasizes federated data ingestion, modular adapters, and the alignment of derived intelligence—enabling cross-agency coordination without requiring raw data consolidation. The architecture integrates satellite imagery (optical and SAR), IoT sensor streams, public alerts, and contextual civic data into a unified, explainable decision-support pipeline. DisasterAI addresses critical challenges in disaster intelligence, including spatial-temporal alignment of asynchronous data, modality-aware fusion, uncertainty representation, and fairness-aware decision-making. Designed to support the entire disaster lifecycle—from early warning and forecast-informed risk analysis to impact assessment and response prioritization—it operates within a human-in-the-loop decision-support context. A scenario-driven evaluation illustrates how DisasterAI enhances coordination effectiveness, improves prioritization consistency, and maintains robustness under partial data availability. By focusing on architectural behavior and operational integration rather than algorithmic benchmarking, this work positions federated, explainable AI systems as a viable foundation for scalable and reliable disaster-response frameworks in complex, data-constrained environments.

The rapid advancement of generative AI raises serious questions about potential differences in story construction between human and AI narratives, particularly in terms of cultural and social artifacts. The research addresses the gap in feminist stylistic studies on AI-generated fiction by conducting a comparative analysis of feminist representations in AI-generated and human-written fiction. By analyzing these narratives, the current research sheds light on the extent to which AI-generated short stories stylistically compare to human-written short stories in terms of feminism. The research is guided by two questions: How do the linguistic choices used in AI-generated and human-written short stories, when analyzed through a feminist lens, reflect or challenge patriarchal thinking? And what are the main similarities and differences between AI-generated and human-written short stories in respect to feminist portrayal? The analysis employs Mills' (1995) feminist stylistic model, with emphasis on endearment terms, metaphor, transitivity, fragmentation, and focalization. The research examines one human-written short story titled Dinner Conversation (2020) and one AI-generated short story titled The Crack in the Bowl (2026) using a carefully standardized prompting process. The findings indicate that both stories perpetuate traditional gender hierarchies, albeit through diverse linguistic mechanisms. According to the research, AI, specifically ChatGPT-5.2, is more progressive in terms of gendered assumptions than the human author. In human-written stories, patriarchy is more pervasive and stable, whereas in AI-generated stories, it is more nuanced and sometimes contradictory. This research adds to the emerging studies on AI storytelling by demonstrating how AI-generated fiction can both duplicate and disrupt traditional gender stereotypes.

documents.abstract: Generative AI is rapidly reshaping STEM higher education. Not only are our educational practices changing, but how we think about educational transformation must also adapt. Existing models of institutional change in STEM, aimed at interactive engagement, have largely followed an adoption logic: relatively stable, well-researched educational practices are evaluated and then scaled. These assumptions do not hold for generative AI, which is an arrival technology – entering classrooms before a sufficient pedagogical evidence base could form, and requiring institutions to act under uncertainty. Building on recent decades of work on STEM education institutional change, we propose a framework identifying six dimensions along which prior models of change must be adapted in light of AI: three concerning the tools at the center of reform (the tool’s evidence base, rate of change, and scope), and three concerning the people involved in change (faculty, change agents, and students). For each dimension, we examine how AI-era assumptions differ from those underlying prior STEM education reforms and derive design implications, including: privileging humble and local inquiries; organizing reform around pedagogical approaches rather than specific tools; repositioning change agents as facilitators of collective inquiry; and engaging students as partners in reform. Collectively, the six dimensions and design implications constitute a framework for adapting change models to support institutions under conditions of genuine uncertainty. Finally, we illustrate how the framework may be applied through a brief case-study of a faculty workshop series carried out in a university physics department to support instructors adapting to this modern AI era.

Understanding how cardiomyocyte structure governs contractile function is fundamental to cardiac biology and disease modeling, yet current approaches rely on time‐resolved imaging and computationally intensive analysis. Here, we present a generative artificial intelligence (AI) framework that directly predicts contractile behavior of human‐induced pluripotent stem cell‐derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC‐CMs) from single static images. Our approach integrates a U‐Net‐based generator with a patch‐based generative adversarial network (GAN) discriminator to translate morphological and sarcomere structural features into pixel‐resolved contraction heatmaps. To further enhance performance and generalizability, we incorporated synthetic cell–function pairs generated via a StyleGAN2 framework, improving prediction accuracy and perceptual similarity. Region‐specific and whole‐cell analyses revealed that AI predictions capture biologically meaningful structure–function relationships, with sarcomere organization strongly associated with both contractile output and prediction fidelity. Reconstruction error emerged as an interpretable metric reflecting localized inefficiencies in sarcomere‐to‐contraction coupling. Together, this framework establishes a scalable, interpretable strategy for inferring cardiomyocyte function from static morphology, eliminating the need for time‐lapse imaging, and positions generative AI as a powerful tool for bridging cellular structure and function to advance high‐throughput phenotyping and in vitro cardiac modeling.

One of the biggest cybersecurity dangers is phishing websites, which trick users into providing confidential information through fake interfaces. Traditional detection solutions, such as black-list and rule-based methods, are no longer effective against emerging attacks. To address the limitations of existing approaches, this study proposes an integrated machine learning system based on URL and host-based characteristics, designed to improve generalization and avoid data leakage. The proposed model uses two branches, each training a separate classifier on a different feature set (URL and host). These branches are combined using a leakage-resistant Out-Of-Fold (OOF) stacking mechanism that derives meta-features from unseen data. In addition, interaction-based meta-features are added to further boost predictive power. The UCI Phishing Websites Dataset, containing 11,055 instances and 17 selected features, was used to evaluate the model. The experimental results validate the proposed hybrid model, which achieves an accuracy of 92.67\% and an ROC-AUC of 0.9788, outperforming the single feature-based models. Cross-validation shows good generalization with low variance. Feature importance analysis shows that the interaction-based meta-features are highly influential in improving classification accuracy. The model achieves a strong balance between performance, computational efficiency, and interpretability compared with contemporary approaches. Its leakage-resistant design enables unbiased evaluation and real-world applicability in cybersecurity. This work contributes to phishing detection research through hybrid ensemble learning with an emphasis on methodological rigor and extensive performance evaluation.

Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials cover broad configurational and chemical spaces, but their reliability can vary across the atomic environments encountered during a simulation. Here we introduce the calibrated Mahalanobis (CALM) extrapolation grade $γ$, a piecewise differentiable per-atom quantity integrated into GRACE foundation models and evaluated alongside energies and forces in a single model pass. We define $γ$ from nearest-cluster Mahalanobis distances in latent feature space, setting $γ=1$ from the training-distance distribution separately for each element and cluster. Controlled tests show that a normalized random projection of the invariant many-body basis detects structural and chemical extrapolation. On different foundation datasets, OMat24 and SMAX, $γ$ correlates with atomic force errors and separates structures with different error distributions. The CALM grade adds percent-level computational cost, and its spatial gradient guides uncertainty-biased data collection toward configurations with larger absolute force errors.

This article is devoted to the development of methodological approaches to wetsuit design based on the classification of water sports. The goal of this research is to create innovative wetsuits adapted to the specifics of water sports, increasing reliability and protective properties, while improving comfort and performance. The subject of the study is the "person-wetsuit-aquatic environment" system, with a particular focus on protecting the wearer from external factors by developing rational variants of wetsuit components, taking into account ergonomics and the dynamic conformity of the product. The article proposes a systematic classification of aquatic sports, taking into account the nature of the aquatic environment, the degree of its control, temperature parameters, and the requirements for protective equipment. A model for the combination of the type of sports discipline and the characteristics of wetsuits (neoprene thickness, design, and mandatory application conditions) has been developed. Special attention was paid to the water sport "slalom" as a sport with maximum hydrodynamic variability and increased thermal protection requirements. The dependence of equipment selection on temperature ranges, flow velocity, and wind conditions has been substantiated. The presented classification can be used in the development of new types of wetsuits with enhanced protective properties, as well as in athlete training, regulatory requirements, and improvement of training logistics.

Traditional scientometric analysis methods primarily rely on binary keyword associations, which limits the ability to capture complex research structures. This study proposes a multi-association rule-based method (MAR) that enables the extraction of higher-order (n-ary) associations among keywords to address the stated limitation. The method integrates the Apriori algorithm with knowledge graph visualization to quantitatively analyse multi-keyword associations. The proposed method is applied to the Building Information Modelling (BIM) research domain. The bibliometric data, comprising 12,185 publications, is retrieved from the Scopus database following a systematic refinement of the initial search results to the architecture, engineering, construction, and operation (AECO)-relevant literature. The results demonstrate that the MAR method effectively identifies complex research patterns. The framework advances traditional scientometric tools by enabling the identification of multi-keyword semantic associations with quantified strength metrics (support, confidence, lift). Emerging trends revealed by the regression analysis include the convergence of BIM with generative artificial intelligence, real-time data integration, explainable AI, and human-centric approaches. The findings provide a scalable and analytical approach for identifying interdisciplinary research trends and gaps. The proposed method enables a deeper understanding of complex knowledge structures while supporting strategic decision-making and technology adoption.

Future fighter operations are expected to combine increasingly capable autonomy, collaborative aircraft, dense sensor information, and sustained physiological and cognitive demands. This Perspective proposes a pilot-wellness-informed ecological framework in which the pilot, a pilot-specific digital twin, an intelligent flight-management system, the aircraft, and external agents are treated as interdependent elements within a systems-of-systems framework. The framework does not replace situation awareness, distributed cognition, joint cognitive systems, adaptive automation, or human-autonomy teaming. Instead, it extends their unit of analysis by making the pilot’s dynamic physiological and neurocognitive state, longitudinal variability, and health-related constraints explicit system variables and design objectives. The pilot digital twin is defined narrowly as an individualized state-estimation and forecasting capability, whereas the intelligent flight-management system integrates pilot, platform, mission, and environmental information to provide explainable recommendations and, where authorized, bounded adaptive action. We identify testable propositions concerning individualized prediction, adaptive support, shared situation awareness, trust calibration, and governance. The framework is prospective and requires validation in simulation, training, and operationally representative environments. Its purpose is to organize research toward systems that protect pilot agency, sustain performance, and preserve long-term health while exploiting increasingly autonomous teammates.

Electronic learning (e-learning) or online learning in medical education has become increasingly prevalent, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, poor student engagement and reduced motivation are among the critical challenges associated with online learning. The e-learning for Renal Applied Pharmacology (e-RAP) is a new technology-enhanced learning tool that includes a nephron image augmented with several Quick Response (QR) codes. It allows students to access relevant QR-linked educational materials prepared by the teachers. This quasi-experimental pilot study examined whether use of the e-RAP tool was associated with differences in cognitive performance, engagement, and motivation among 105 preclinical medical students at Universiti Sultan Zainal Abidin (UniSZA), Malaysia. Participants in the intervention group (Year 2, n = 45) used the e-RAP tool, while the control group (Year 1, n = 60) received conventional teaching. Cognitive performance, engagement, and motivation scores were measured using pre- and posttest multiple-choice questions (MCQ), the Burch Engagement Survey for Students, and the Motivated Strategies for Learning Questionnaire, respectively. Both groups demonstrated improvements in mean cognitive scores from pre- to post-test MCQ, with greater gains in the intervention group than in the control group. The intervention group was also associated with higher emotional and cognitive engagement (both in and out of class) and higher scores in several motivational domains, including intrinsic value, cognitive strategy use, and selfregulation. Although groups differed by academic year, baseline knowledge was comparable. Taken together, these preliminary findings suggest that e-RAP use may be associated with differences in cognitive performance, engagement, and motivation.

The evolving dynamics of security management have necessitated the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in predictive intelligence and military operations in Africa. This integration presents a paradigm of significant opportunities alongside profound challenges. Theoretically, AI promises to enhance situational awareness, enable results-oriented conflict management, and optimize operational efficiency across the continent. However, this study posits that its deployment is fraught with daunting ethical and practical impediments specific to the African context. This work interrogates the ethical imperatives of AI in predictive intelligence and military operations in Africa. To achieve its objectives—which include defining context-specific ethical principles, diagnosing implementation barriers, and proposing a practical framework—the study adopted a mixed-methods approach. This methodology relied on semi-structured interviews with military personnel, defence analysts, and AI ethics scholars, complemented by a historicist content analysis of secondary sources including policy documents, institutional reports, and academic literature. The findings reveal a strong consensus among stakeholders on the paramount importance of ethical principles such as accountability, transparency, fairness, and meaningful human oversight. However, the study identified that the realisation of these principles is severely constrained by critical obstacles, including a stark infrastructure and data deficit, a pervasive regulatory and policy vacuum, and pre-existing governance frailties. These contextual challenges amplify ethical risks, particularly algorithmic bias and accountability gaps, threatening to exacerbate social divisions and undermine human security. Consequently, the study concludes that ethically responsible AI use is not an automatic outcome but must be actively cultivated. It recommends, among other measures, the urgent development of a continent-wide regulatory framework by the African Union to harmonise standards and prevent misuse. The study argues that only through such deliberate, multi-faceted interventions—combining robust regulation, strategic investment in digital infrastructure, and international collaboration on equitable terms—can Africa harness the benefits of AI for security while safeguarding fundamental ethical imperatives.

The EU AI Act (Art. 27) requires deployers of high-risk AI systems to conduct Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments (FRIAs) before deployment, yet the evidence needed for credible assessments is fragmented across incompatible incident repositories, risk vocabularies, and legal texts. We present a reusable Semantic Web-based framework that consolidates this evidence for two high-risk public sector categories: employment and worker management (Annex III(4)) and access to essential public services (Annex III(5)(a)). A curated 150-record corpus is annotated along four axes using keyword, LLM, and hybrid methods and serialised as a SPARQL-queryable knowledge graph of 1,351 RDF triples. Five FRIA demonstration scenarios surface 103 records (68.7% coverage). Evaluation against a 69-record gold standard reveals that LLM-assisted classification of the employment domain achieves only $κ= 0.045$, a cautionary result for automated fairness-related evidence retrieval in this domain. All artefacts are released openly to support adoption by regulators, national authorities, and SMEs.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Abstract Despite the increasing adoption of automated/autonomous guided vehicles (AGVs) in precision agriculture, existing human-machine interfaces (HMIs) remain function-centric, frequently neglecting the cognitive and user experience (UX) needs of non-technical operators. Consequently, current dashboards suffer from limited usability, high cognitive load, and reduced system transparency, increasing the risk of operator error. To address this gap within agricultural teleoperation interface design, this study presents a theory-driven HMI framework that systematically translates Endsley’s Situational Awareness (SA) theory (Perception, Comprehension, Projection) and ISO 9241 ergonomic principles into a structured three-panel AGV teleoperation interface. Unlike conventional function-oriented dashboards, the proposed framework organises interface components according to operator cognitive requirements to support information perception, comprehension, and projection during remote operation. A theory-driven agricultural teleoperation HMI framework was developed by translating cognitive and ergonomic principles into practical interface organization strategies. To formatively evaluate this SA-driven design architecture, we conducted a user-perception study with non-expert digitally literate participants (N = 20), evaluating three iterative HMI prototypes. The comparative results indicate that the SA-aligned layout received higher user ratings in perceived decision-support capability (SA3), cognitive workload reduction, and overall usability compared with baseline designs during formative evaluation. The study provides preliminary methodological guidance for agricultural teleoperation HMI design, while recognizing that objective operational validation with target agricultural users remains necessary.

Data-driven machine learning (ML) techniques have become an essential tool in many domains of science. Their application to atomistic simulations of matter is particularly widespread and impactful. This success is due largely to the existence of a well-developed and established physics-based modeling framework, ranging from first-principles electronic-structure calculations to molecular dynamics and statistical sampling, into which ML was integrated naturally to reshape long-standing trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and scale. Nevertheless, this integration raises both conceptual and practical challenges, from choosing between data-centric and physics-based modeling approaches to adapting established software stacks to modern hardware accelerators and ML libraries. As the field evolves rapidly, fueled in part by widespread enthusiasm but also by tangible impact, it seems appropriate to take a moment to consider the current state of the art and open challenges, and reflect on what can be done to better coordinate efforts across the community. With this goal in mind, several members of this community met in Lausanne in January 2026 at CECAM to discuss algorithms, models, software and hardware infrastructure, and the most promising scientific applications that have become possible thanks to the use of artificial intelligence in atomic-scale simulations. This strategic roadmap paper summarizes the outcomes of these discussions, suggesting some long-term goals, and some concrete actions, to establish a healthy, sustainable and impactful atomistic ML ecosystem.
topics: Advanced Electron Microscopy Techniques and Applications

documents.abstract: Background: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping English-as-a-foreign-language (EFL) writing instruction, yet the mechanisms through which AI integration may improve written English proficiency (WEP) remain theoretically fragmented. Objective: This systematic review synthesises literature published within the 2018–2026 review window, together with foundational theoretical works, to develop a structural-equation-modelling (SEM) framework in which self-regulated learning (SRL), learner engagement, self-efficacy, and AI literacy operate as parallel and serial mediators between AI integration and WEP. Method: Following a structured thematic-synthesis approach, the reviewed literature was organised around four connected domains: AI-supported writing instruction, generative-AI adoption, learner and teacher perceptions, and self-regulated learning in AI-supported contexts. The synthesis then examined evidence for direct, mediating, and serial relationships among the focal constructs. Key findings: The literature provides partial support for the individual links connecting AI integration, the proposed mediators, and language-learning outcomes; however, these pathways are rarely tested within a single integrated model. Evidence for mediation remains fragmented, the proposed serial chain is largely untested, and Jordanian and broader Levantine contexts remain under-represented relative to East Asian and Gulf settings. Implications: The review proposes fourteen hypotheses: nine direct-effect hypotheses (H1–H9) and five mediation hypotheses (H10a–H10e), including one serial mediation chain, as a framework for future quantitative validation among English majors at public Jordanian universities.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: People are one of the important resources in any industry. Therefore, their health and safety are essential for overall well-being. Various ceramic factories expose workers to various occupational health risks because of their distinct manufacturing processes. This study focused on identifying various health hazards among ceramic workers in selected units of the Bulandshahr district of Uttar Pradesh. The aim of this study was to assess the occupational health hazards experienced by ceramic workers in specified ceramic factories in the region and to evaluate measures for improving their health and safety. A cross-sectional quantitative study was conducted using the purposive sampling method from December 2025 to June 2026 on 80 workers from different units of the ceramic industry in Bulandshahr. Both male and female workers from ceramic industry were included. A self-developed, structured, and undisguised questionnaire on occupational health hazards was prepared to collect data directly from the respondents through face-to-face surveys. This study revealed occupational health hazards among ceramic workers. Most participants were male, 85% and female, 15%. Psychological hazards were most reported (82.5%), followed by ergonomic (56.25%), physical (32.5%), biological (27.5%), and chemical hazards (26.25%). Of the studied workers 45% suffered from these hazards in which 40% of the workers suffered from musculoskeletal problems and only 5% were suffered from respiratory problems. To make the things in favor of workers, there is a need for workload management where reasonable working hours, counselling sessions, and breaks to reduce stress should be fixed. Regular training and awareness programmes should be conducted for workers to educate them about mental health and stress management.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces
Indoor Air Quality and Microbial Exposure

documents.abstract: Abstract The World Wide Web has evolved from a predominantly static information environment into an increasingly interactive, semantic, distributed and intelligent digital ecosystem. The earlier study on Web 1.0 to Web 3.0 described the transition from the read-only web to the read-write social web and then toward the semantic web. This revised study extends that framework to Web 4.0 and examines the technological and conceptual changes across the four stages. Web 1.0 is characterized by static pages, one-way information delivery and limited user participation; Web 2.0 emphasizes interaction, user-generated content, social networking and web applications; Web 3.0 is associated with semantic interoperability, decentralized architectures, data ownership and intelligent processing; and Web 4.0 is increasingly discussed as an intelligent or symbiotic web in which artificial intelligence, Internet of Things (IoT), cloud/edge computing, augmented and virtual reality, machine-to-machine communication and autonomous agents can interact with people and each other. The literature does not provide one universally accepted definition of Web 4.0, so this paper treats it as an emerging research and technology paradigm rather than a fixed technical standard. The study also discusses implications for libraries and information services, including intelligent discovery, personalized services, virtual assistance, semantic knowledge organization and human-machine collaboration. The paper concludes that the movement from Web 1.0 to Web 4.0 represents a shift from information access toward participation, meaning, intelligence and increasingly symbiotic interaction.

The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare systems is rapidly increasing in India, with the market estimated to grow from $0.83 billion in 2023 to $17.75 billion by 2032. Employee satisfaction remains a major concern that relevant studies in the healthcare sector have yet to address. This article explores how AI integration is affecting employee satisfaction in India’s healthcare industry. The healthcare industry faces a 60% shortage of digital skills; 47% of Indian healthcare workers are not digitally literate, and only 34% of organizations are advancing toward piloting AI projects, despite 86% having adopted AI. Implementation challenges include limited technical expertise among clinicians, the psychological burden of increased monitoring, poor rural infrastructure, data privacy concerns, and workforce constraints. For AI to succeed, it must be presented as a supplement to workers, not a replacement. This shift should include targeted training to address digital literacy gaps, governance that incorporates clinician input in system design, and ongoing staffing support. Existing evidence suggests that AI adoption may be associated with burnout and reduced employee satisfaction when it is not coupled with these integrated efforts. Beyond technical expertise, research highlights human-centered design, thorough training for healthcare professionals, and maintaining autonomy as key drivers of effective AI integration in healthcare in India. To benefit from AI, healthcare facilities in India must adopt modern technology. They must also prioritize staff well-being.
